Headquarters: Remote Roles - EMEA

Who We Are

At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom.

OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves.

Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er.

About the Opportunity

OKX is hiring a Head of Tax Information Reporting to build and run our global tax information reporting function. The function covers the OECD Crypto-Asset Reporting Framework (CARF), the EU's DAC8 directive, the amended Common Reporting Standard (CRS 2.0), FATCA, and US Form 1099-DA across multiple reporting entities and a large global user base, with annual reporting across the EU, Brazil, and other CARF jurisdictions.

Most of the work is data: getting the right user, transaction, and balance data out of our platform, reconciling it, and turning it into accurate filings. You will own the relationship with our reporting vendor, the data specification that feeds it, and the quality checks that decide whether a file goes out.

You will run a central function that owns policy, data, vendor, QA, and submission for every entity in scope. Each reporting entity names an accountable signatory. Local compliance and entity leads are consulted on local requirements and support registration where the law requires a local filer. You will work closely with Product, Data Engineering, Finance Operations, Group Tax, Legal, Data Privacy, and the local entity leads.

Location: remote available, with a strong preference for the US or EU. Some travel to OKX offices.

What You'll Be Doing

• 

Own the end-to-end CARF, DAC8, CRS 2.0, FATCA, and 1099-DA reporting cycle for every OKX entity in scope: population definition, self-certification coverage, data extraction and reconciliation, file production, QA, filing, corrections, and tax authority queries.

• 

Define and own the data specification that feeds the tax platform vendor: which users, which transactions, which balances, how they are aggregated by user and jurisdiction, and how they reconcile to the ledger. Work with Product and Data Engineering to build and test the pipeline.

• 

Build and run the QA framework. Reconcile every file to source, validate it against the OECD XML schema and local variants, sample-test self-certification reasonableness checks, and run cross-entity consistency checks for users who hold accounts with more than one OKX entity. Nothing files without your release.

• 

Manage the tax platform vendor: contract scope, delivery calendar, test cycles, output validation, issue resolution, and the annual renewal decision.

• 

Set the group reporting policy and interpret the regimes for OKX: reportable crypto-assets, transfers to unhosted wallets, staking and reward income, retail payment thresholds, residency tie-breakers, and TIN rules, exercising independent technical judgment, supported by Legal and external tax advisers.

• 

Own the global tax self-certification design in onboarding, including validation rules, refresh triggers, and the backlog remediation program for existing users, working with Compliance and Product.

• 

Define the process for restricting undocumented accounts under DAC8 and CARF, including reason codes and customer communications, with restrictions applied automatically in Product and monitored by the central team.

• 

Maintain the entity-by-entity readiness tracker covering domestic enactment, registration, self-certification coverage, and deadlines. Report weekly to the CCO and monthly to the CARF steering committee.

• 

Hands-on leader. Build a small, senior team, scaled through the reporting vendor and outside advisers. Coordinate with and train local compliance and entity leads.

• 

Support independent testing by Compliance Monitoring, Risk, and Internal Audit, and support tax authority examinations with complete, reproducible records.

What We Look For In You

• 

7+ years in tax information reporting, tax operations, or regulatory data reporting at a global exchange, broker, bank, fintech, or digital asset platform, including at least 3 years leading a team.

• 

Hands-on experience in a global, distributed digital asset business: you have worked with exchange or wallet transaction data, multiple legal entities, and users spread across many jurisdictions. This is required.

• 

Strong data skills. You can write SQL, define data specifications for engineers, reconcile large transaction datasets to a ledger, and find the gap when the numbers do not tie. You have built or run data quality controls on reporting output.

• 

Working knowledge of CARF, DAC8, CRS, and FATCA, including due diligence rules, self-certification requirements, reportable transaction categories, and the XML schemas used for exchange. Direct CARF or DAC8 implementation experience is strongly preferred given live DAC8 obligations and upcoming CARF reporting.

• 

Experience managing a tax reporting vendor or reporting platform, including scoping, testing, and holding the vendor to a delivery calendar. the tax platform vendor experience is a plus.

• 

Experience building a function from a small base: writing the policy, designing the controls, hiring the team, and running the first cycle.

• 

Ability to explain data and tax issues plainly to executives, engineers, and local compliance officers, and to run a steering committee.

• 

Judgment on when to escalate, comfort working across US, EU, and Asia time zones, and a record of meeting hard filing deadlines.

Nice to Haves

• 

Experience with US Form 1099-DA or 1099-B production, backup withholding, or Qualified Intermediary reporting.

• 

Experience with the DAC8 60-day account restriction process or equivalent undocumented account remediation at scale.

• 

Familiarity with GDPR requirements for sharing customer data with tax authorities, including data protection impact assessments.

• 

Python or similar scripting for data validation, and experience with data warehouse tools such as Databricks.

• 

Experience working inside a Three Lines Model, including supporting second-line monitoring and Internal Audit.

• 

A CPA, chartered tax adviser, or equivalent; or a degree in data science, computer science, or accounting.

Perks & Benefits

• 

Competitive total compensation package

• 

L&D programs and Education subsidy for employees' growth and development

• 

Various team building programs and company events

• 

Comprehensive healthcare schemes for employees and dependants

• 

More that we love to tell you along the process!

OKX Statement:

OKX is committed to equal employment opportunities regardless of race, color, genetic information, creed, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, lawful alien status, national origin, age, marital status, and non-job related physical or mental disability, or protected veteran status. Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, we will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Notice:

All official OKX vacancies are published on this website. While roles may appear on selected third-party platforms from time to time, information on other sites may be inaccurate or outdated. If in doubt, please apply directly through our official careers website.

Information collected and processed as part of the recruitment process of any job application you choose to submit is subject to OKX's Candidate Privacy Notice.

Headquarters: Remote - Israel

Join the company that’s building the telemetry infrastructure for the AI era. At Cribl, we partner with IT and Security teams at many of the world’s biggest enterprises, including half of the Fortune 100, to bridge the gap between AI ambition and infrastructure reality. As the AI Platform for Telemetry, we give customers the choice, control, and flexibility to manage and analyze telemetry for both humans and agents, so they can build what’s next.

We’re one of the fastest‑growing private companies and a leading player in a massive, fast‑moving market. With a global workforce, we’re remote‑first and grounded in a simple idea: software is a people business. Cribl is the place where curious, collaborative people can do their best work, grow fast, and bring their full selves to the herd.
Why You’ll Love This Role

Cribl Detect brings Cribl’s telemetry platform and security expertise together to help customers improve detection coverage, reduce alert noise, and speed investigations—while keeping the flexibility to use the tools they already have. As Director of Security Research, you’ll build and lead a research organization across detection engineering, threat hunting, and AI-driven triage and investigation. You’ll develop the team, set research priorities, and partner with Product and Engineering to shape Cribl Detect. You’ll also publish technical research and collaborate with Cribl’s internal SOC to strengthen Cribl’s defenses.

Based in Israel, this hybrid role works closely with teammates across Israel and the US, with regular overlap with US working hours and periodic travel to the US. The package includes competitive compensation and equity, pension and Keren Hishtalmut contributions subject to local policy, paid time off, a Cibus meal card, and professional development.

As An Active Member Of Our Team, You Will…

• Build and lead the research organization: hire and develop researchers and research leaders, set shared standards, and align priorities with customer needs, emerging threats, and product goals.

• Own threat-informed detection content and effectiveness by turning threat intelligence into validated rules and hunt packs, maintaining coverage, fidelity, telemetry readiness, and rule health, and delivering timely threat advisories.

• Guide AI-driven investigations by defining how agents test hypotheses, gather evidence, distinguish malicious from legitimate activity, and escalate uncertainty; partner with Engineering to evaluate accuracy, completeness, and false-negative risk.

• Lead telemetry and security-tool research: define evidence needs and tool capabilities, study how telemetry collection and transformation affect security outcomes, and guide data requirements and integrations.

• Shape security methods and evaluation for additional AI-agent workflows, including MITRE mapping, noise tuning, and rule authoring.

• Build technical credibility through substantive publications, practitioner guides, presentations, and selected public tools, frameworks, or datasets.

• Partner with Cribl’s internal SOC on detections, threat hunts, investigation methods, and security validation; use operational feedback to improve research and product quality while respecting the SOC’s operational ownership.

• We are a remote-first company and work happens across many time-zones – you may be required to occasionally perform duties outside your standard working hours.

If You’ve Got It - We Want It

• 10+ years in security research, detection engineering, threat hunting, or investigation, including 5+ years leading teams and a record of turning research into customer-facing content or product capabilities.

• Experience hiring and developing researchers, growing technical leaders, and building collaborative teams.

• Strong understanding of adversary behavior, MITRE ATT&CK, security telemetry, detection validation, and analyst workflows.

• Experience guiding AI agents across security workflows and evaluating output accuracy, security effectiveness, and appropriate human oversight.

• Practical knowledge of security tools, APIs, and data limitations, with the ability to review detection logic and investigative methods and validate ideas through queries, scripting, or prototypes.

• Strong cross-functional leadership and communication skills, including the ability to prioritize research and influence Product, Engineering, customers, and executives.

• Willingness to travel internationally, including to the US.

• Bonus: Experience spanning detection engineering and automated investigation, or developing investigative guidance or evaluation datasets for AI agents.

• Bonus: Experience with cloud attack paths, identity, workload security, or cloud-native telemetry; substantive publications, conference presentations, or open-source security contributions are also valued.

• Bonus: An open, low-ego communication style and an appreciation for good—or bad—jokes.

GitLab is the intelligent orchestration platform for DevSecOps. GitLab enables organizations to increase developer productivity, improve operational efficiency, reduce security and compliance risk, and accelerate digital transformation. More than 50 million registered users and more than 50% of the Fortune 100* trust GitLab to ship better, more secure software faster.

The same principles built into our products are reflected in how our team works: we embrace AI as a core productivity multiplier, with all team members expected to incorporate AI into their daily workflows to drive efficiency, innovation, and impact. GitLab is where careers accelerate, innovation flourishes, and every voice is valued. Our high-performance culture is driven by our values and continuous knowledge exchange, enabling our team members to reach their full potential while collaborating with industry leaders to solve complex problems. Co-create the future with us as we build technology that transforms how the world develops software.

*Fortune 500® is a registered trademark of Fortune Media IP Limited, used under license. Claim based on GitLab data. Fortune 100 refers to the top 20% ranked companies in the 2025 Fortune 500 list, published in June 2025. Fortune and Fortune Media IP Limited are not affiliated with, and do not endorse products or services of GitLab.

An overview of this role

At GitLab, People technology never stands still, and as a People Systems Engineer, you’ll build what keeps it moving. Reporting to the Senior Director, People Technology, and working alongside our Lead People Systems Engineer, you’ll design, build and maintain the automations, integrations and AI-powered workflows that connect Workday, Greenhouse, Slack and the tools that power our global workforce. You’ll own features from request through tested code, deployment and ongoing reliability across Workato, Google Cloud and Claude. With an AI-forward mindset, you’ll rethink how People work gets done, eliminating manual effort and creating streamlined, delightful experiences for team members. If you think like a software engineer, love solving puzzles and want to grow your career at the intersection of people systems, AI and automation in an all-remote, async-first environment, this is your role.

What You’ll Do  

  • Build, test and maintain People system automations and integrations across Workato, Google Cloud Platform, Claude, Workday, Greenhouse and GitLab, owning your features from design through deployment.
  • Develop integrations between Workday, Greenhouse, Slack and internal tools using Workday Web Services (WWS) and Slack’s API and Bot SDK, and build Slack apps and bots that turn manual steps into simple, automated workflows for team members around the world.
  • Write clean, readable automation code in Ruby or a comparable scripting language, stored and versioned in GitLab, with clear documentation and peer code reviews.
  • Keep pace with a high-growth company by monitoring integration health, troubleshooting failures quickly and fixing root causes so our automations stay reliable at scale.
  • Ship changes safely through GitLab CI/CD pipelines, following testing, change-management and Sarbanes-Oxley (SOX) IT general controls (ITGC) standards with care.
  • Lead with AI: use AI tools, large language models (LLMs) and Model Context Protocol (MCP) frameworks, including Claude, every day to accelerate development, prototype AI agents and reimagine how People work gets done, then share what you learn so the whole team moves faster.
  • Look past the surface of a request to find the real problem, then recommend and build solutions that are durable, scalable and easy to support. Partner with People Technology Analysts on configuration, testing and releases, and with Information Security, IT and AI Engineering on security and standards.
  • Raise the bar for how automations are architected, documented and maintained, learning from and contributing alongside our Lead People Systems Engineer.

What You’ll Bring 

  • Hands-on experience building automations or integrations, ideally with human resources or business systems.
  • Experience writing and maintaining code in Ruby or a comparable scripting language, such as Python or JavaScript, and a willingness to learn Ruby if you haven’t already.
  • Hands-on experience with Workato or a comparable integration platform as a service (iPaaS) in a production environment.
  • Experience working with APIs and web services, including REST and SOAP, and an understanding of how data moves between systems.
  • Proficiency with Git for version control and code review; you treat automation code like production software.
  • A forward-thinking, AI-forward mindset: you use AI tools every day to automate tasks, speed up development and improve processes, and you’re energized by what AI makes possible next.
  • The ability to work independently, solve problems with curiosity, come with options and a recommendation, and collaborate openly. You protect highly confidential information and take ownership of code quality, reliable outcomes and the end user’s experience.
  • Additional relevant experience includes Workday integrations (WWS, Reporting as a Service or Workday Studio), Slack apps or bots, CI/CD pipelines, Google Cloud Platform or Amazon Web Services, Docker or Kubernetes, building with LLMs, AI agents or MCP frameworks, SOX ITGC controls, Greenhouse, Serval, Google Workspace, or all-remote and asynchronous work. A related computing degree or equivalent experience is also welcome; none of these is required.

About the team

The People Technology team is building the systems foundation that lets GitLab scale as a global, all-remote company. We’re always raising the bar for what People technology can do, improving reliability, usability and intelligence across the platforms that power our People organization. We work across core systems, integrations, reporting and compliance, and partner closely with stakeholders across time zones to move fast, build with purpose and create seamless experiences that empower people to do their best work. If you want to grow your career building something that matters at a company working at the edge of what’s possible, this is the team.

How GitLab will support you

  • Benefits to support your health, finances, and well-being
  • Flexible Paid Time Off 
  • Team Member Resource Groups
  • Equity Compensation & Employee Stock Purchase Plan
  • Growth and Development Fund
  • Parental leave 
  • Home office support
